{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative bias (e.g., -0.25 or below) to counteract over-optimism.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — model tends to overreact.",
    "When true price spikes occur, reduce forecast overshoot by applying a 10-15% dampening factor to subsequent 3-5 day predictions.",
    "In periods with sustained negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment values), shift forecast mean toward historical 15-day average to avoid overcorrection.",
    "For sentiment history with increasing positivity (e.g., 0.00 → 0.33 → 0.50), gradually increase forecast bias upward, but cap at +10% above recent 15-day mean to avoid runaway spikes.",
    "If model consistently underpredicts in high-sentiment periods (e.g., sentiment > 0.50), apply a +5% upward bias to forecast mean for next 3 days.",
    "In cases where true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (e.g., >15% underprediction), apply a corrective offset equal to 1.5x the deviation to next forecast.",
    "When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast is consistently above true outcome, reduce forecast by 5-10% for next 2 days to avoid overestimation."
  ]
}
